title: The Great Emu War
sources: National Museum of Australia, 'The Great Emu War' (November 1932, Western Australia; military deployed after emus damaged wheat crops; ~20,000 emus targeted)
Australian War Memorial records: soldiers with Lewis guns fired ~2,500 rounds; 2,500 emus reported killed; emus 'won' the campaign
Contemporary reports (1932): emus outran the soldiers, split into small groups, often 'unscathed'; the military withdrew after a few weeks

lines.text: In nineteen thirty-two, Australia declared war on birds.
Thousands of emus were eating the farmers' wheat crops.
So the government sent soldiers with machine guns to fix it.
But the emus had other plans.
They split into small groups and outran the army.
The soldiers fired thousands of rounds, mostly missing.
One soldier said the emus were like tanks.
lines.caps: One soldier said | the emus | were like *tanks.

lines.text: After a few weeks, the military gave up and went home.
And Australia never tried to fight birds again.
lines.caps: Australia never | tried to fight | *birds again.
